projects.name: Pixelorama

language.source: br godot-stagehand-growth-distribution-87s.18 — GDScript, no .csproj; Stagehand was installed into and run against a real Pixelorama checkout at 93c0bef7

godot_version.source: project.godot at 93c0bef7 declares config/features=PackedStringArray("4.6") — minor only, no patch. The earlier 4.6.3 claim was wrong; 87s.20 and 87s.21 both repro'd on Godot 4.6.2, so 4.6.x is what has actually been exercised

license.source: LICENSE at 93c0bef7 reads 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2019-present Orama Interactive and contributors'

axes.source: own-cli-parser VERIFIED (br 87s.20 — host rejected --stagehand). embedded-subwindows VERIFIED (br 87s.21 — modal AcceptDialog splash at /root/Control/SplashDialog). content-scale VERIFIED BY OBSERVATION ONLY (87s.18 saw /root content_scale_factor = 1.5 at runtime) but NOT declarable from project.godot — 93c0bef7 has no stretch/content_scale keys at all, so Pixelorama sets it programmatically as a UI-scale preference. large-project is DOUBTFUL: 21 MB and 1362 tracked files at 93c0bef7 is not large, and the axis needs re-measuring by actual import time rather than repo size. Unassigned but evidenced: heavy-autoloads — project.godot declares 13 autoloads

projects.notes: Candidate #1; already earned its place — 87s.20, 87s.21 and the content_scale_factor finding all came from driving this project. SETTLED at 93c0bef7 from a local checkout (br 87s.18): project.godot IS at the repo root (no project_subdir needed); there are NO git submodules (the earlier report was wrong — the checkout step needs no --recurse-submodules); LICENSE is MIT; 13 autoloads. STILL OPEN: (1) the pin is not on a tag — git describe gives v1.1.10-156-g93c0bef7, i.e. 156 commits past the last tag, committed 2026-07-23, so enabling this entry requires either pinning back to a real tag or amending the doc's no-branch-shaped-ref rule to 'SHA is authority, ref is prose'; (2) whether to reassign axes — heavy-autoloads is now evidenced here and large-project is not, which would change what the other candidates are needed for, so it is left alone pending review. NOT AN AXIS THIS PROJECT COVERS: warnings-as-errors. Pixelorama's project.godot only DISABLES two warnings (gdscript/warnings/return_value_discarded=false, narrowing_conversion=false) and sets no gdscript/warnings/*=2, so it cannot reproduce the host-strict-warnings failure that broke plugin.gd and editor/setup_panel.gd during Asset Library prep.

axes.source: own-cli-parser evidenced by rodzill4.github.io/material-maker/doc/command_line.html documenting --export-material/--target/-o; embedded-subwindows is inferred from it being a dialog-heavy desktop tool and is a guess

projects.notes: Second independent own-cli-parser data point, on a different Godot minor than Pixelorama. CAVEAT: both it and Pixelorama document a '--' user-args convention, which suggests get_cmdline_user_args() rather than raw argv — so an unknown --stagehand before '--' may be swallowed by the engine rather than rejected by the app. That distinction is unverified and is precisely what this project is here to settle.

projects.name: OpenGamepadUI

language.source: snippets described it as a GDScript Godot 4 project; settle by checking for a .csproj at the pinned SHA

godot_version.source: snippets said only 'Godot 4' with no minor. The 4.3 recorded here is a PLACEHOLDER INTENT, deliberately chosen to match a minor already in the manifest so it cannot inflate the claimed version spread. Read config/features in project.godot and correct it before enabling

license.source: snippets say GPLv3-or-later; settle by reading LICENSE at the pinned SHA. Note this is the only copyleft candidate — cloning it in CI is fine, but confirm before relying on it

axes.source: custom-input is strongly suggested by its README describing a gamepad input system that remaps gamepad input to mouse and keyboard input, which implies _input/_unhandled_input interception. Settle by grepping for _input/_unhandled_input at the pinned SHA

projects.notes: The only candidate with real evidence for the custom-input axis, which matters because an app that intercepts input at _input is the one most likely to swallow Stagehand's synthesized events. RISK: it reportedly depends on ShadowBlip GDExtensions and a Linux X11/ALSA build toolchain, making it the heaviest CI cost of the set. If that proves prohibitive, the axis needs a different owner rather than being dropped.
